title: Caching, cookies, CORS and versions
summary: The headers that make the web fast, stateful and (mostly) safe, and how HTTP/2 and /3 differ.

steps.title: Cache-Control
body: Responses tell caches (browser, CDN, proxy) what they may do:
```text
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600     anyone may cache it for 1 hour
Cache-Control: private, max-age=60      only the user's browser, 1 minute
Cache-Control: no-cache                 may store, but must revalidate every time
Cache-Control: no-store                 never store (bank statements)
ETag: "v42"                             a version tag for revalidation
**Revalidation**: the client sends `If-None-Match: "v42"`; if unchanged, the server answers `304 Not Modified` with no body.
The *age* of a cached response is how long ago it was received; it is **fresh** while `age < max-age`.

steps.prompt: You deploy new `app.js` but users keep running the old version for hours. Its response has `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`. The standard fix?
options: Put a content hash in the file name (`app.3f9a2c.js`) and keep the long max-age
Ask users to clear their cache
steps.explain: Fingerprinted names make each version a new URL: cache forever, and the HTML (served with `no-cache`) points at the new name.

steps.title: A cache-control evaluator
prompt: Write `string Decide(string cacheControl, int ageSeconds)` returning:
- `"revalidate"` if they contain `no-cache`, or if there's no `max-age`, or if `ageSeconds >= max-age`
Directives are comma-separated, case-insensitive, with optional spaces: `"Public, MAX-AGE=600"`.
hints: Find the directive starting `max-age=` and parse the rest.

steps.title: Cookies
body: HTTP is stateless. **Cookies** add state: the server sets one, the browser sends it back on later requests to that site.
```text
Set-Cookie: session=abc123; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=3600
Cookie: session=abc123
- `HttpOnly`: JavaScript can't read it (limits XSS damage).
- `Secure`: only sent over HTTPS.
- `SameSite=Lax/Strict/None`: whether it's sent on cross-site requests (CSRF defence). `None` requires `Secure`.

steps.prompt: Match each cookie attribute to what it protects against.

steps.title: CORS
body: Browsers enforce the **same-origin policy**: a page from `https://app.shop.example` may not read responses from `https://api.shop.example`
(a different *origin* = scheme + host + port) unless the API opts in with **CORS** headers.
For "non-simple" requests (e.g. JSON `POST`, custom headers) the browser first sends a **preflight**:
```text
OPTIONS /orders
Origin: https://app.shop.example
Access-Control-Request-Method: POST
204 No Content
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.shop.example
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST
CORS is enforced **by the browser only**. `curl` and server-to-server calls ignore it, which is why "it works in Postman" proves nothing.

steps.prompt: Order a cross-origin JSON POST from a browser.
lines: Page calls fetch() with a JSON body
Browser sends OPTIONS preflight with Origin
Browser lets the page read the response
steps.explain: If the preflight answer doesn't allow the origin/method, the real request is never sent.

steps.prompt: Match each HTTP version to its key property.
pairs: Text, one request at a time per connection
Binary frames, many streams over one TCP connection
Runs over QUIC on UDP; no TCP head-of-line blocking

steps.title: CORS check
prompt: Write `bool AllowCors(string origin, string method, List<string> allowedOrigins, List<string> allowedMethods)`.
Origins match exactly (case-insensitive), except an allowed entry `*` matches any origin. Methods match case-insensitively.
Also write `string OriginOf(string url)` that returns scheme + host + port only (`https://app.shop.example:8443/x` gives `https://app.shop.example:8443`).
starter: bool AllowCors(string origin, string method, List<string> allowedOrigins, List<string> allowedMethods)
solution: bool AllowCors(string origin, string method, List<string> allowedOrigins, List<string> allowedMethods)
template: Dojo.Eq("wrong origin", false, AllowCors("https://evil.example", "GET", dojoO, dojoM));
Dojo.Eq("wrong method", false, AllowCors("https://app.shop.example", "DELETE", dojoO, dojoM));
Dojo.Eq("wildcard", true, AllowCors("https://x.example", "GET", new List<string> { "*" }, dojoM));
hints: For the origin, find the first `/` after `://`.
